# Instana On-Prem SNMP & Tivoli Monitoring Setup

## When This Skill Activates

Activate when the user asks about:
- Connecting an Instana host agent (self-hosted / on-premises) to SNMP devices
- Collecting metrics from IBM Tivoli Monitoring (ITM V6 / ITCAM V7) into Instana
- Setting up OpenTelemetry Collector with SNMP receiver for Instana
- Creating a custom dashboard in Instana UI for SNMP or ITM metrics
- Troubleshooting SNMP metric collection or ITM sensor in Instana

---

## Architecture Overview

Two supported collection paths:

```
Path A (SNMP direct):
  SNMP Devices ──SNMP──► OTel Contrib Collector ──OTLP HTTP──► Instana Host Agent ──► Instana Backend ──► Dashboard

Path B (IBM Tivoli Monitoring):
  ITM V6/ITCAM V7 Agents ──ITM Sensor──► Instana Host Agent ──► Instana Backend ──► Dashboard
```

---

## Step 1 — Clarify Use Case

Use `ask_followup_question` to determine:
1. **Collection path**: SNMP direct (Path A) or IBM Tivoli Monitoring ITM V6 (Path B), or both?
2. **SNMP version**: v1 / v2c (community string) or v3 (user/auth/priv)?
3. **Instana backend**: already installed and running on-prem? If not, direct the user to the
   [self-hosted installation docs](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/instana-observability/standard) first.
4. **Network topology**: is the OTel Collector on the same host as the Instana agent, or a separate host?

---

## Step 2 — Path A: SNMP via OpenTelemetry Contrib Collector

### 2a. Download OTel Contrib Collector

Direct the user to download the appropriate binary for their OS/arch from:
`https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases/releases`

```bash
# Linux amd64 example
wget https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases/releases/download/v0.115.0/otelcol-contrib_0.115.0_linux_amd64.tar.gz
tar -xzf otelcol-contrib_0.115.0_linux_amd64.tar.gz
```

### 2b. Generate Configuration File (`host-snmp.yaml`)

Use `write_file` to create `/opt/otelcol/host-snmp.yaml` with the following template
(ask the user to supply: device IP, SNMP version, community string, and OIDs to collect):

```yaml
receivers:
  snmp:
    collection_interval: 60s
    endpoint: "udp://<DEVICE_IP>:161"
    version: v2c                        # or v1 / v3
    community: "<COMMUNITY_STRING>"
    oids:
      - name: "system.uptime"
        oid: "1.3.6.1.2.1.1.3.0"
        unit: "ticks"
        metric_type: gauge
      - name: "if.in.octets"
        oid: "1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.10"
        unit: "By"
        metric_type: sum
        is_scalar: false
        indexed_value_prefix: "if"
      - name: "if.out.octets"
        oid: "1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.16"
        unit: "By"
        metric_type: sum
        is_scalar: false
        indexed_value_prefix: "if"

processors:
  batch:
  resource:
    attributes:
      - key: service.name
        value: "snmp-tivoli-host"
        action: upsert

exporters:
  otlphttp:
    endpoint: "http://<INSTANA_AGENT_HOST_IP>:4318"
    tls:
      insecure: true
  debug:
    verbosity: detailed

service:
  pipelines:
    metrics:
      receivers: [snmp]
      processors: [batch, resource]
      exporters: [otlphttp]
```

### 2c. Enable OTel in Instana Host Agent

Add to `<agent_install_dir>/etc/instana/configuration.yaml`:

```yaml
com.instana.plugin.opentelemetry:
  grpc:
    enabled: true
  http:
    enabled: true
```

If OTel Collector runs on a **different host** than the agent, also add to
`<agent_install_dir>/etc/instana/com.instana.agent.main.config.Agent.cfg`:

```properties
http.listen=*
```

### 2d. Run OTel Collector as a systemd Service

Use `write_file` to create `/etc/systemd/system/otelcol-snmp.service`, then run:

```bash
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now otelcol-snmp
sudo systemctl status otelcol-snmp
```

---

## Step 3 — Path B: IBM Tivoli Monitoring V6 (ITM Sensor)

> ⚠️ The old Integration Proxy is **deprecated March 2026, removed June 2026**.
> Only the ITM Sensor (built into the Instana host agent) is supported.

### 3a. Enable ITM Sensor in Instana Host Agent

Add to `<agent_install_dir>/etc/instana/configuration.yaml`:

```yaml
com.instana.plugin.ibm-itm:
  enabled: true
  listen_port: 8080
  mode: dual      # dual = sends to both TEMS and Instana; instana = Instana only
```

Restart the Instana host agent after the change.

### 3b. Point ITM V6 Agents to Instana

On each ITM V6 / ITCAM V7 agent, add the Instana host as a secondary destination:

```bash
-c dual -p <INSTANA_AGENT_HOST>:8080
```

---

## Step 4 — Verify Data Flow

Run `execute_command` to check the agent log for incoming SNMP / ITM data:

```bash
tail -f <agent_install_dir>/log/agent.log | grep -i "snmp\|itm\|otel"
```

For OTel debug output, check the collector log:
```bash
journalctl -u otelcol-snmp -f
```

Expected success indicators:
- OTel collector: `"Successfully exported metrics"`
- Instana agent log: `"Received OTLP metrics"` or `"ITM sensor: received payload"`

---

## Step 5 — Create Custom Dashboard in Instana UI

Walk the user through:

1. Open Instana UI → **Infrastructure** — confirm devices appear as **OTEL Host** entities.
2. Click **My Custom Dashboards** → **Create Dashboard** → enter a name.
3. Click **Add Widget** → choose widget type (Chart, Big Number, Table, Pie).
4. Set **Data Source** = `Infrastructure & Platforms`.
5. In **Metric** field, search for collected SNMP metrics:
   - `snmp.system.uptime`
   - `snmp.if.in.octets`
   - `snmp.if.out.octets`
   - For ITM: search by the ITM attribute name
6. Use **Add Filter** → `service.name = snmp-tivoli-host` to scope results.
7. Click **Create** → **Save Changes**.

---

## Troubleshooting Reference

| Symptom | Check |
|---|---|
| No metrics in Instana UI | Verify OTel endpoint IP/port; check `http.listen=*` if remote host |
| OTel collector exits immediately | Check YAML indentation; run with `--config host-snmp.yaml` manually |
| SNMP timeout errors | Confirm SNMP is enabled on device; verify community string and firewall port 161/UDP |
| ITM sensor not receiving data | Confirm `listen_port` not blocked; verify ITM agent `-c dual` flag |
| Agent cannot connect to backend | Use `stanctl agent apply --agent-endpoint-host agent-acceptor.<domain> --agent-endpoint-port 8443` |
